name: makersuite-inline-video-resolution
purpose: MAKERSUITE inline video media AND the gemini-3 mediaResolution gate. Pinned: `part.type === 'video_url'` calls addDataUrlPart(url, 'video/mp4', detail) (src/prompt-converters.js:565-568), and inside addDataUrlPart the resolution is GEMINI_MEDIA_RESOLUTION[detail] || null (:519), appended as `part.mediaResolution = { level }` ONLY when /gemini-3/.test(model) (:529-533). GEMINI_MEDIA_RESOLUTION maps low -> media_resolution_low and high -> media_resolution_high, with 'auto' deliberately unmapped (:28-32). So the provider part is { inlineData: { mimeType, data }, mediaResolution: { level: 'media_resolution_high' } } in that member order. Its sibling makersuite-inline-image.json differs only in the media type and the model, so the mediaResolution member is attributable to the gemini-3 gate rather than to video.
stage1Boundary: Stage 1 validates the backend -> provider transformation only. Browser-side prompt assembly happens in the frontend before the request reaches the route and is NOT covered here; a green provider-wire capture is not evidence of preset-level equivalence.

tier2.reason: The mock listens on an ephemeral loopback port, so the authority is not a property of either backend.
tier2.harnessSource: tools/mock-provider/main.go: --port 0 asks the kernel for a free port

tier2.rule: the recorder origin is replaced with <mock>
tier2.reason: API_MAKERSUITE is a pinned literal, so the GoTavern leg reaches the recorder through its seam and the pinned leg through this transport redirect. The PATH and the ?key= parameter are untouched and ARE compared.

tier2.rule: recorded verbatim; the payload is a data: URL, so no authority is substituted and no fetch is involved
tier2.reason: The media reaches the provider INLINE. It is a data: URL on purpose: addDataUrlPart only accepts a url that startsWith('data:') (src/prompt-converters.js:516) and nothing is fetched for this source, so the peer receives the exact bytes the pinned converter embedded and the probe cannot reach the network (doctrine 6). A remote http(s) URL would be silently DROPPED by that guard rather than fetched, which would make the scenario pass while proving nothing.

tier3.reason: It is a measurement of elapsed wall-clock time, so it differs on every run and no backend can match it; the value is a duration, not a contract.
